messages:
sam: heads up — our eu-west canary is failing health checks, traffic getting 502s from the proxy. noticed after the 11:10 deploy :thinking_face:
deploy-bot: deploy/service/@canary finished (eu-west1): rollout=5/10, status=unhealthy
lina: which check is failing? ALB target health or the app ping?
sam: ALB target group shows unhealthy, failing on /health (timeout). pods themselves show OK on curl localhost:8080/health inside node.
rahul: did anyone change the ingress source CIDR or the security group rules for the proxy pods?
jordan: I pulled VPC flow logs for the node subnet, grep for DENY around 11:10 — seeing a bunch of rejects to nodeport ranges 32768-61000 from 44.122.0.0/16 (albs)
rahul: exact flow log snippet:
```
REJECT TCP src=44.122.53.21:443 dst=10.24.7.56:32770 action=REJECT rule=ACL-172
REJECT TCP src=44.122.53.22:443 dst=10.24.7.57:32772 action=REJECT rule=ACL-172
```
sam: so ALB healthcheck source IPs are hitting nodeports but NACL is denying ephemeral port range. did we recently tighten the ingress NACL?
lina: checked network-acl ACL-172 — looks like a change last night to deny ephemeral > 32768 -> 65535 from outside CIDR to enforce egress-only policy, probably intended for some subnet but applied broadly.
jordan: confirm: this NACL is associated with the edge node subnet (where kube-proxy maps nodeports) — that would drop ALB -> node health probes.
rahul: workaround: update NACL to allow TCP 32768-61000 from 44.122.0.0/16 (ALB ranges) and re-evaluate. long-term we should move to SG-based ALB -> ENI path or switch to target-type=ip so healthchecks hit endpoints not nodeport.
sam: can someone flip the rule? i'm oncall and can take it if y'all agree.
lina: +1. I'll prepare the change and post the exact aws cli command.
rahul: CLI to allow range (example):
```
aws ec2 replace-network-acl-entry --network-acl-id acl-0abc123 --rule-number 172 --protocol 6 --port-range From=32768,To=61000 --egress false --rule-action allow --cidr-block 44.122.0.0/16
```
lina: applied patch at 11:23, rolling health checks now.
deploy-bot: target/blue-canary: healthy=6/10 unhealthy=4/10 -> 9/10 after update
sam: confirm tests: curl to nodeport from a jumping host in the ALB CIDR now succeeds.
jordan: I also added a temporary guard in infra playbook to ensure NACL changes require a tag check to avoid broad ephemeral denies. filed infra-ops#142 for follow-up.
rahul: follow-up actions: (1) add playbook test to block only specific external cidrs, (2) evaluate switching ALB to ip-targets for this service, (3) audit NACL changes last 30 days.
oncall-bot: reminder: if we roll back the NACL in rollback window, contact oncall+infra.
sam: thanks all — canary now stable, marking incident resolved. :thumbsup:
